paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God's word is not the same as somebody's dream, and it's not the same as somebody saying "The LORD declares it." The LORD asks, "For what is straw compared to grain?" (Jeremiah 23:28). Straw looks nice in the bowl, but you can't bake a single cookie with it.

The LORD can't be fooled either. He asks, "Can a man hide in secret places where I cannot see him?" and then, "Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?" (Jeremiah 23:24). He says the prophets who spoke lies were not sent by Him, and they were "of no benefit at all to these people" (Jeremiah 23:32). Attaching His name to your own words does not make them His, and He knows the difference every time.

So what do you do with that, baker? You go to the source. The LORD says to ask, "What has the LORD answered?" and "What has the LORD spoken?" (Jeremiah 23:35). His word is "like fire" and "like a hammer that smashes a rock" (Jeremiah 23:29), so read it for yourself, and let it be the loudest voice in your kitchen. This passage ends a group of two, but the teaching is not over.
